nodes.label: AI Agency and the Bureaucratic Niche (Harari)
nodes.summary: Harari: AI won't need robots. It lives in the paperwork and trust systems we already built, and it takes control there.

nodes.label: AI Frontier and Geopolitics
nodes.summary: Anthropic's case: AI leadership compounds. Compute sets the pace, and the next few years decide who stays ahead.

nodes.label: Boredom and the Default Mode Network
nodes.summary: Phones kill boredom, and boredom is when your brain gets around to asking what your life means.

nodes.label: Building Agents (OpenAI Framework)
nodes.summary: The question is never whether you can build an agent. It's whether the workflow needs one.

nodes.label: Decision Making & Cognitive Biases
nodes.summary: We judge on what we can see and ignore what's missing. It's why confident people look competent.

nodes.label: Demis Hassabis on AGI and AI Drug Discovery
nodes.summary: Hassabis puts AGI at 2030, give or take a year. Still missing: reliability, memory and long-term planning.

nodes.label: Hackman - Conditions for Team Effectiveness
nodes.summary: We credit leaders for what the team's structure did, because leaders are visible and structure isn't.

nodes.label: Iain McGilchrist on Value and the Sacred
nodes.summary: McGilchrist: we shrank the word value down to money and power. Truth, goodness and beauty got left out.

nodes.label: Leadership & Teams
nodes.summary: Sinek: a leader's first job is protecting the people inside the circle. Strategy and results come after.

nodes.label: LLMs as Human Surrogates (DK AI Study)
nodes.summary: LLMs match the average person, not any one person. Synthetic market research has to beat cheap baselines.

nodes.label: Nobody Knows What Is Going On (Mollick)
nodes.summary: Nobody has the AI playbook, including the labs. So writing your own is an advantage.

nodes.label: Teaching Through Engagement (Mark Rober)
nodes.summary: You can't teach anyone without their attention. Get it with something remarkable, then attach the lesson.

nodes.label: We Already Have AGI (The Context Problem)
nodes.summary: By 2009 standards we already have AGI. Enterprise AI fails because the agent never got what the veteran knows.

nodes.label: The Deployment Gap - My AI Career Thesis
nodes.summary: AI capability is outrunning adoption. The bottleneck is the last mile, and that's the work I want to do in energy.

nodes.label: You Can't License a Brain
nodes.summary: Licensing your brain per use is a nice dream. Knowledge fails the tests that make something ownable.

nodes.label: AI Agents and Workflow Execution
nodes.summary: Most white-collar work runs on clicking buttons, and agents can now click buttons.

nodes.label: AI in the Wild
nodes.summary: What people building with AI in real businesses are doing, collected one conversation at a time. No demos.

nodes.label: AI Safety Slow-Down and the China Race Problem
nodes.summary: Every AI slow-down plan assumes US-China cooperation that isn't coming.

nodes.label: Bond Valuation
nodes.summary: A bond's price is its future payments discounted at the yield the market demands. Everything else moves that yield.

nodes.label: Capital Asset Pricing Model
nodes.summary: Diversification kills firm-specific risk, so you only get paid for market risk. Beta measures how much you carry.

nodes.label: Capital Structure
nodes.summary: With no taxes or frictions, the debt mix doesn't matter. Real firms get a tax shield until distress costs eat it.

nodes.label: Cost of Capital
nodes.summary: Leverage changes how the return splits between debt and equity. The size of the return stays the same.

nodes.label: Customer Lifetime Value
nodes.summary: How much is a customer actually worth? That number sets the ceiling on what you can spend to win one.

nodes.label: dcf-valuation
nodes.summary: An asset is worth its future cash flows, discounted for risk. Comps and multiples are shorthand for this.

nodes.label: Deadweight Loss
nodes.summary: A trade's surplus doesn't depend on the price. Value gets lost when good trades don't happen or bad ones do.

nodes.label: Dopamine and Motivation
nodes.summary: Dopamine fires in anticipation of reward. Short-form video trains your brain away from waiting for one.

nodes.label: Double Marginalization
nodes.summary: When manufacturer and retailer both mark up, the chain sells too little. Both earn less and customers pay more.

nodes.label: Efficient Market Hypothesis
nodes.summary: You can beat the market, just not reliably with what everyone already knows.

nodes.label: Elasticity of Demand
nodes.summary: Measure price sensitivity in percentages, never dollars. On a straight demand line it changes at every point.

nodes.label: Embodied Leadership
nodes.summary: Gut responses and physical cues carry real signal. Treat them as one more input to a decision.

nodes.label: Energy Transition Field Notes
nodes.summary: Long-duration storage has a magic number: about 100 hours at about $20/kWh. Lithium-ion is still above $100.

nodes.label: Equity vs Credit Investing
nodes.summary: Two bets on one company. Equity says the market underrates the upside. Credit says it overrates the downside.

nodes.label: Free Cash Flow Model
nodes.summary: Same logic as the dividend model, for companies that don't pay dividends. Discount free cash flow instead.

nodes.label: Jevons Paradox and the AI Labor Demand Question
nodes.summary: My hypothesis: cheaper AI means the world wants more of that work, the way cheaper coal meant more coal burned.

nodes.label: Marginal Revenue
nodes.summary: Selling one more unit means cutting the price on everything you already sell. So marginal revenue sits below price.

nodes.label: MBA Key Insights
nodes.summary: The ideas from the MBA I could explain at dinner without notes. Everything else stays in the course notes.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.summary: Understanding is memory. Connect a new idea to what you know and explain it to yourself, or it won't last.

nodes.label: Nash Equilibrium
nodes.summary: Nobody can do better by changing only their own move. When the answer depends on how they'll respond, draw the board.

nodes.label: NPV and IRR
nodes.summary: IRR is what the project earns. WACC is what it needs to earn. NPV is the dollars of value from the difference.

nodes.label: Pivot or Perish Simulation
nodes.summary: A five-year retail sim: run a legacy department store losing share. The only score is market value at the end.

nodes.label: porter-five-forces
nodes.summary: Industry profits come from the bargaining environment, not from how hard the incumbents work.

nodes.label: Portfolio Diversification
nodes.summary: Investors can diversify cheaply themselves, so a firm diversifying for them usually destroys value.

nodes.label: Price Discrimination
nodes.summary: Charging buyers different prices needs two things: buyers who value it differently, and no resale between them.

nodes.label: Product Differentiation
nodes.summary: The less customers will switch, the further above cost you can price. Brand and lock-in pay off that way.

nodes.label: Purpose vs Profit When They Truly Conflict
nodes.summary: When purpose and profit diverge for good, which one wins and who decides in advance? Most answers deny the conflict.

nodes.label: Speed vs Human Sustainability
nodes.summary: How much human cost can a leader spend to move fast? The bill arrives after the leader has been promoted.

nodes.label: The Five Layers of Trust
nodes.summary: Saying AI kills consulting, or that trust saves it, is lazy. Trust has five layers that erode at different speeds.

nodes.label: The Modeling-Operating Gap in PE
nodes.summary: Smaller PE shops overpay because the people setting the assumptions have never run the asset.

nodes.label: Time Value of Money
nodes.summary: Money at different dates can't be compared directly. Every valuation in corporate finance is this idea applied.

nodes.label: World Models
nodes.summary: LLMs predict the next word. World models predict what happens next in the world. It may be a different kind of intelligence.

nodes.label: Financial Modelling
nodes.summary: A valuation is a process that gives a range, never a single number. And profit isn't cash.

nodes.label: GMAT Lessons
nodes.summary: Three attempts and hundreds of hours. What I learned about studying under pressure outlasted the score.

nodes.label: Career Narrative
nodes.summary: Engineer, then energy transition specialist, then MBA. The next step is the part I'm working out.
